clue.text: Mr Sloan entertaining a straight type was sycophantic

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the jockey's first name holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Tod Sloan was a famous American jockey, whose name gave rhyming slang 'on your tod' (alone)
a die is the hard stamp that strikes type or coins

explanation.surface: Some Mr Sloan, playing host to an upright sort, was fawning over him.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadying is crawling flattery, so to have done it is to have behaved obsequiously.

clue.text: Raised border in brass

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word lifts it bottom to top, so it reads backwards

parts.note: to abut is to border on something

explanation.surface: A raised brass edging, as on a piece of ornamental metalwork.
explanation.definitionFit: The tuba is the deepest instrument of the brass section, so brass names its family.

clue.text: Where demonstrators face bank, ghee is thrown: so one's very much 3 when 12

indicators.note: something thrown is tossed about, so all these words are jumbled into the long saying

explanation.surface: A protest by a riverbank turns messy as clarified butter is hurled about.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references read 'very much in mind when out of sight', the gist of the proverb. 'is thrown' shuffles all thirty letters of 'Where demonstrators face bank, ghee'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says that being apart makes love stronger, so the absent one stays firmly remembered when unseen.

clue.text: Purposed to get pub ready for detonation, according to report

indicators.note: a report is what is heard, so the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: a pub is an inn, and one rigged with explosives is mined

explanation.surface: A plot to rig a pub with explosives, as gossip has it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something purposed is intended, and to have a plan in mind is to intend it.

clue.text: Name of president who died an old man?

parts.note: d is the standard abbreviation for died, as in family trees
wight is an archaic word for a person or creature

explanation.surface: Asking which head of state passed away in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: Dwight Eisenhower was a US president.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the first name of Eisenhower, the 34th President of the United States.

clue.text: Knight held a feast first

indicators.note: first places the feast ahead of the word for held, reversing their order in the clue

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion or celebration
had means held or possessed

explanation.surface: A knight who hosted a banquet before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad was the purest Knight of the Round Table in Arthurian legend.

clue.text: Player a la Potter makes good start at Middle Eastern capital, securing points

indicators.note: the abbreviation for good stands at the start of the rest
securing means holding fast, so the capital clasps the points within it

parts.note: Amman is the capital of Jordan
E and S are compass points, east and south

explanation.surface: A player in the style of Potter gets a good start in Jordan's capital, picking up points.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Potter wrote 'Gamesmanship', the art of winning by bending the spirit of the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamesman uses legal but sly tricks to win, the ploys Stephen Potter described.

clue.text: Supposed origin of president's diary in taxi at home

parts.note: a log is a daily record
a cab is a taxi
in means at home

explanation.surface: Tracing a leader's beginnings through a diary left in a cab at home.
explanation.walkthrough: Presidents such as Lincoln were famously said to have been born in such a humble dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The log-cabin birth was the classic rustic origin story claimed for American presidents like Lincoln.

clue.text: See 2
Soldiers picked out for objectivity?

definitions.meaning: a unit of troops selected and sent off on a separate task
impartial aloofness, free of personal involvement

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a body of troops detailed for duty and a cool, unbiased standpoint.

clue.text: Sweeper from El Salvador replacing Romania with another

indicators.note: replacing swaps one set of letters for another within the word

parts.note: another sweeper, taken as a broom
RO is the international vehicle code for Romania
ES is the international vehicle code for El Salvador

explanation.surface: A broom imported from El Salvador takes the place of a Romanian one.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a broom made of twigs bound to a handle, a traditional sweeping tool.

clue.text: I'm getting money for the road as I enter the country

parts.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written MI
a grant is a sum of money given

explanation.surface: Someone collects travel money as they cross the border.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: One who arrives to settle in a foreign land is described by entering the country.

clue.text: Cool cuties hit annus horribilis

indicators.note: Latin for horrible, so the words are mangled horribly into a new order

explanation.surface: Sweet things are struck by a dreadful year, recalling the Queen's annus horribilis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Annus horribilis' (horrible year) was the Queen's phrase for 1992; here 'horribilis' scrambles CUTIES HIT ANNUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool reception is a lukewarm one, showing a lack of eager interest.

clue.text: Has a duty, keeping so fit, mysteriously to be hidden

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the duty word holds the scrambled letters

parts.note: ought means is obliged, has a duty

indicators.note: mysteriously signals that so and fit are mixed up in a puzzling way

explanation.surface: Someone obliged to keep in shape somehow wants to be concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has a duty' looks like a statement about someone, but it is one verb: ought. 'mysteriously' is the anagram signal for 'so fit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unseen or concealed is said to be not visible at all, the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: Turn to law to get moorland shrub

parts.note: a U-turn is a turn, giving U
lex is Latin for law

explanation.surface: A legal turn yields a plant of the heath.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulex is the botanical name for gorse, a spiny shrub of heaths and moors.

clue.text: Edition of verse with a Brazilian spirit

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city, gives RIO
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A book of poetry published with a cachaça-style Brazilian drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A variorum is an edition of a text that gathers the notes and readings of many editors.

clue.text: Oil producer enters destined to be hammered

indicators.note: enters puts the reworked oil inside the word for destined

parts.note: fated means destined

indicators.note: a producer makes something new from material, so the letters of oil are refashioned

explanation.surface: An oil company joins a venture fated to be crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil producer' looks like a company or a well, but 'producer' is the anagram signal for the word before it; 'hammered' describes metal beaten into leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliated metal has been beaten into thin leaves, the work of hammering.

clue.text: Young goatherd who fancied Nancy?

definitions.meaning: a young lad tending billy goats, read whimsically
Bill Sikes was Nancy's lover in Dickens's Oliver Twist

explanation.definitionFit: The name of the folk-song suitor, taken also literally as a boy minding billy goats.

clue.text: The "Creation" is golden — a high spot I love

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
a tor is a rocky hilltop
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Praising Haydn's work as a golden summit that the speaker adores.
explanation.walkthrough: TOR is a rocky hill, a word common in Devon's Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: Haydn's The Creation is a large sacred work for soloists, choir and orchestra, an example of this form.

clue.text: One of a pair has time to succeed

parts.note: to win is to succeed

explanation.surface: Half of a couple gets the time to triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin is one of two born together, so it is half of a matched couple.

clue.text: Agreement when dispatched

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sent means dispatched

explanation.surface: Approval given at the moment the letter was posted.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is consent or approval, a formal yes.

clue.text: River where the king couldn't stand the heat?

indicators.note: the saying is 'if you can't stand the heat, get out of the kitchen', so the king leaves

parts.note: the room where heat is proverbially unbearable
K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

explanation.surface: Asking at which river a monarch found things too hot.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb tells those who can't take pressure to leave the kitchen; take K out of KITCHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Itchen is a chalk-stream river in Hampshire, flowing through Winchester to Southampton.

clue.text: Focusing on one effect of noise is capital

indicators.note: the result produced from these words is a rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: Concentrating on one effect of a din turns out to be excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money or a city, but it is just fodder with NOISE and IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Specialisation means concentrating on a single area of skill or study.

clue.text: Record is complete in part

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the words, running across them

explanation.surface: A record that is only partly finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, and here it sits inside the words of the clue.

clue.text: Find somewhere to sit within reach

definitions.meaning: to secure a place at a table, as in a restaurant

explanation.definitionFit: Read as three words it is securing a seat; hyphenated it means accessible.

clue.text: I went on a pilgrimage to reverse the priority of holy war

indicators.note: the front part and the back part of the word swap places

parts.note: jihad is a holy war

explanation.surface: A pilgrim explains that holy war comes second to devotion.
explanation.walkthrough: JI moves from the front of JIHAD to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A hadji is a Muslim who has made the pilgrimage to Mecca, so speaks of having gone.

clue.text: When the gracious appear to make a point in a study?

indicators.note: to make is to form, so the letters are formed into a new word

parts.note: E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: A researcher makes a point in a study about polite people.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme says 'Tuesday's child is full of grace', so that is the day the gracious are born.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme, the child born on this weekday is full of grace.

clue.text: Hindu achievement of instant riches without trendy females

indicators.note: without means lacking, so these letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written; that its middle letters also run unbroken to the answer is a coincidence of the deletion
in means fashionable
shes are females, the plural of she

explanation.surface: A Hindu path to quick wealth, minus fashionable women.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove IN, then S and HES, from INSTANTRICHES to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tantric describes the esoteric Tantra traditions within Hinduism.
